Exported activities from *-internal modules and app/src/internal ship only in the internal flavor (internalImplementation). Release exports are browser entry points (IntentDispatcher, BrowserActivity, SystemSearch, SelectedText*, Settings, NewTabSettings); BrowserActivity is exported without a filter and its extra handling needs manual review.
The only exported service is the Custom Tabs CustomTabsService; it records sessions, returns false/FAILURE for postMessage, receiveFile and updateVisuals, and exposes no sensitive data or actions.

kotlin.random.Random/java.util.Random are used only for sampling, delays, download IDs, notification IDs and PendingIntent request codes; keys, IVs, PKCE verifiers and WireGuard keys use SecureRandom.
Security-relevant values (AES keys, IVs, RSA keys, PKCE verifier, WireGuard keys) are generated with SecureRandom/KeyGenerator/KeyPairGenerator, not time-based sources.
AES keys are 256-bit (KeyGenerator init 256, PBKDF2 256, 32-byte random); RSA key pairs use 2048 bits.
Cipher transformations are AES/GCM/NoPadding and RSA-OAEP-SHA256; no DES, 3DES, RC4 or Blowfish found.
Symmetric encryption uses AES/GCM; no bare "AES" or ECB symmetric transformations. RSA/ECB/OAEP is out of scope per the test.
The app checks for a secure lock screen via KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure and BiometricManager.canAuthenticate before enabling autofill/sync auth.
No KeyGenParameterSpec purposes are defined; the only asymmetric key pairs (software RSA in Sync) are used solely for RSA-OAEP encryption/decryption.
No getInstance call passes an explicit provider; Cipher, Mac, MessageDigest, KeyGenerator and KeyPairGenerator use the default provider.

No HostnameVerifier is used, but the WebView SSL-error fallback trusts a certificate once its signature chain reaches a bundled Let's Encrypt root, without checking that the leaf matches the hostname or is within validity. A mismatched-host cert that also triggers SSL_UNTRUSTED can therefore be accepted.

evidence.detail: Validation only looks up the issuer by CN and verifies signatures; no hostname or leaf-validity check.

fills.reason: onReceivedSslError decides only on getPrimaryError(): when it is SSL_UNTRUSTED and the chain verifies to a bundled Let's Encrypt root, it calls proceed() without checking other errors (SSL_IDMISMATCH, SSL_EXPIRED) via hasError(). The same pattern is in the URL-extraction WebView.

evidence.detail: Decision based solely on the primary SSL error.
proceed() after the partial chain check.
